territorial_scope.description: Applies to public and private institutions providing essential services and to vital operators in Chile, which must report to the national CSIRT.

evidence.quote: Las instituciones públicas y privadas que presten servicios calificados como esenciales

summary.short: Regulation implementing Law 21.663 (Chile) requires essential-service providers and vital operators to report significant cybersecurity incidents to the national CSIRT: an early alert within three hours, a second report after 72 hours, and a final report within 15 days of the alert.
summary.long: Chile's regulation under Law 21.663 sets reporting rules for significant cybersecurity incidents. Essential-service providers and vital operators must report to the national CSIRT. An incident is significant if it can interrupt an essential service, affect physical integrity or health, affect IT assets or networks even without immediate service impact, enter systems without authorisation, or affect systems holding personal data; the number of people affected, duration and geographic extent are also considered (Art. 3). Reports go through the Agency's platform, which operates 24 hours a day (Art. 8). Reporting is staged: an early alert within three hours of becoming aware of the incident (Art. 9), a second report after 72 hours (Art. 10; 24 hours for a vital operator whose essential services are affected), an action plan within seven calendar days for vital operators (Art. 11), and a final report within 15 calendar days of the early alert once the incident has been managed (Art. 12). Partial reports are due every 15 days for prolonged incidents (Art. 13). Reports must omit personal data (Art. 6). Planned maintenance is not an incident (Art. 4). The Director may exempt incident categories and essential-service providers from notification (Art. 3). Heads of state bodies must require IT service providers to share vulnerability and incident information (Art. 15). The regulation takes effect when the Agency starts its activities (first transitional article).

relations.note: Enabling act. Considerandos 5 and 6 state that the contents of the reports and the notification procedure are to be set by this regulation under the Ley's art. 9 and art. 27.

notes: Enabling act is Ley 21.663. The Vistos also cite DFL 1/19.653 (Ley 18.575), Ley 19.880 and Contraloría Res. 7/2019; the text gives them no operative link, so they are not coded. Inconsistencies: Art. 1 l) defines the Plataforma by reference to Art. 2, which does not mention it (the platform is in Art. 8). Art. 1 k) refers to 'su Reglamento' of the Ley, which appears to be a separate instrument not in this document. Art. 10 contains 'plazo de máximo de setenta y dos horas' (wording only). The section_status entry is included only because the schema requires it; relations are coded in the array.

thresholds.variable_text: participación accionaria del Estado en empresas y sociedades (State ownership stake)
thresholds.measurement: Ownership stake held by the State (éste) in the company; alternative test is majority on the board (mayoría en el directorio), not numeric
thresholds.consequence: The regulation's provisions apply to state companies and companies in which the State holds the stated stake
thresholds.conditions: Alternative to majority in the board of directors (mayoría en el directorio)

evidence.quote: Las disposiciones de este reglamento serán aplicables a las empresas del Estado y sociedades en que éste tenga participación accionaria superior al 50% o mayoría en el directorio.
